conviction_note: Q3 was 80% covered at USD 30,716/day before the quarter ended and the bar (USD 168.7m net, S&P CapIQ via Inderes) sits close to what that coverage builds to, so the quarter decides little. The new line is Q4 coverage, which peers (Ardmore MR USD 57.6k on 45%, Scorpio MR USD 56k, TORM 53% at USD 78.4k) have already shown to be roughly double Q3, and the sector sold those reports (TORM -6.5%/-8.8% on 4-5 Nov). That leaves a slight upside lean, p_up 52, on a 4.5% scale. The findings sum (+0.2) and the scaled number (+0.18) agree, and both are near zero for the same reason: most of what this release carries has been pre-signalled.

findings.finding: Hafnia's own coverage (80% of 9,376 Q3 earning days at USD 30,716/day), the disclosed USD 13.3m JV-sale gain and TORM dividend income build Q3 net profit at roughly USD 170-185m, modestly above the USD 168.7m consensus. Q2's cost base (USD 85.6m from TCE to adjusted EBITDA) and D&A of USD 47.2m were used for the build.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hafnia's quarterly prints have moved little in this stage's window: Q2 2026 +1.30%, Q2 2025 +0.03%, Q2 2024 +3.10% (median of all 8 results-type days 1.41%). Q2 2026 beat on EPS and missed on TCE.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The coverage was published in August and four analysts built the consensus on it. What could be unpriced is the JV gain and TORM dividend sitting on top. If the market expected a beat, the stock would have outrun peers into the print, and it has not: -4.16% over 20 days, in line with the sector selloff.
findings.independence: TORM's Q3 per-day rates (MR USD 36,137, LR1 USD 38,667) were above Hafnia's covered USD 30.7k, so Hafnia's uncovered 20% probably fixed at or above the covered rate: https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/torm-third-quarter-profit-rises. Ardmore's lower MR spot of USD 27,031 cuts the other way: https://www.panabee.com/news/ardmore-shipping-earnings-q4-2026

findings.finding: Q4 coverage, the release's guide-equivalent, will show a step-up from Q3's ~USD 31k/day. Peers fixed Q4 at about twice Q3: Ardmore MR USD 57,600 on 45% against USD 27,031 in Q3; Scorpio MR USD 56k and LR2 USD 181k; TORM 53% of Q4 at USD 78,419. Hafnia's level will be diluted by H2 time-charter cover locked by August (H2 53% at USD 28,917).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sector precedent this season: TORM raised its full-year guide and showed Q4 at USD 78k, yet fell 6.5% and 8.8% on 4-5 Nov against STNG's -2.6% and -5.1%. Ardmore fell about 4% and 7.5% on the same days after its Q4 MR USD 57.6k print. Scorpio rose 3.9% and 7.2% on 28-29 Oct on its Q4 bookings and dividend raise. Beats in this sector have recently been sold.
findings.why_not_priced: Hafnia's own Q4 number has not been published, but the peers' have, and the sector fell on them, apparently on Hormuz-normalisation fears (Kpler, 6 Nov: Hormuz clearance at 69% of pre-war, Atlantic MR rates falling). If the Q4 step-up were unpriced, Hafnia would not have dropped from NOK 100.8 on 29 Oct to 86 on 10 Nov alongside the peers. So only the gap between Hafnia's figure and what peers implied for its mix is unpriced, and its sign is unknown.
findings.independence: Scorpio Q4 to date (LR2 USD 181k on 44%, MR USD 56k on 47%): https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/tankers/scorpio-tankers-quarterly-profit-rises. Ardmore Q4 MR USD 57,600 on 45%: https://www.panabee.com/news/ardmore-shipping-earnings-q4-2026

findings.finding: The September placement added 35,488,875 shares (~7%) at NOK 80, so a 90% payout on ~USD 170-185m works out to about USD 0.28-0.31/share, against the ~USD 0.32 the Inderes/CapIQ consensus reportedly carries for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 lifted the payout to 90% and DPS to USD 0.5003, and the stock rose 1.30% on the day. No measured precedent of a DPS shortfall.
findings.why_not_priced: Only if the consensus DPS was not updated for the placement. The USD 0.32 figure is snippet-only (Inderes preview not fetched), and USD 0.32 x 499m shares = USD 160m = 90% of ~USD 177m, which is what a pre-placement share count would imply. Retail dividend-yield holders in Oslo price on DPS, not on net income.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive against a lean that is near flat (priced_lean +0.21, from the run-up) and a 20-day sector selloff. They do not cut hard against either, because the positive part is pre-signalled by Hafnia's own coverage and by peers whose own beats were sold.
language_note: nothing the English sources did not already carry: Hafnia files on NewsWeb in English only. The Norwegian layer was the NewsWeb category labels (e.g. 'INNSIDEINFORMASJON', 'MELDEPLIKTIG HANDEL FOR PRIMÆRINNSIDERE'), which confirmed no resultatvarsel was filed, and a Nordnet Norwegian summary of the TORM CEO's 'happy' remark ('Ingen av dem lovet en fusjon eller et oppkjøp' = 'neither promised a merger or a takeover'), which the English wires also carried in substance.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the Q3 build rests on coverage disclosed on 28 Aug, so F1 cut from +0.3 to +0.2
'The move is in the guide' / 'too small about the move': Q4 coverage is this release's guide-equivalent and new for Hafnia, so abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5
'A verified fact is not a predicted reaction': sector beats were sold (TORM, Ardmore), so p_up held at 52 rather than moved up
